habitat: Usually in pairs in evergreen forest or adjacent plantations. At high altitudes it occurs only in summer, and in winter it moves to lowland riverine forest and gardens.
summary: A fairly common resident. The only forest bird with scarlet underparts and iridescent green upperparts. The male's breast is green. The female lacks the green breast. The bill is pale yellow, and the identification line says greenish-yellow. Turquoise-blue skin patches show on the head when breeding. The long square tail has white outer feathers. The immature is like the female, with the breast and shoulders lightly barred. The call is a slow hoot-hoot. The Kemp name Narina Trogon and the code RB were left unchanged.

calls.description: In the breeding season, October to December, a low 'hoot-hoot… hoot-hoot… hoot-hoot', repeated slowly. The grade A call is from the Wilge River valley in Gauteng. The filename is XC607366-2020-12-06 06_16NarinaTrogon.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a fairly common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. It leaves high altitudes in winter. Scarlet-red is stored as red. The bill is pale yellow and greenish-yellow, so yellow is stored and the second wording is kept in the bill note. The grade A call is from Gauteng. The iNaturalist account has no display name, so the login sitszasadam is credited. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.
